chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, from the completion of the greeting for the one who is resident is the handshake, and the completion of the greeting for the traveler is the embrace.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to greet someone who is traveling versus someone who is at home according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a nuanced social etiquette where the form of greeting adapts to the recipient's state of residence versus travel, reflecting the Prophet's tradition of varying physical greetings based on context. In Shia scholarly tradition, this distinction highlights the importance of attentiveness to the emotional and physical needs of others, as travelers often require more affectionate gestures (mu'anqah) to alleviate the hardship of journey, while the settled (muqim) are greeted with the standard handshake (musafaha).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From the complete welcome for the staying one (not travelling), is the handshake, and the complete greeting (السَّلَامُ) upon the traveller is the hugging’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The completion of greetings of peace for one at home is to shake hands and for one on a journey it is to hold him in one’s arms.”
